units.title: The New Science
units.blurb: Gilbert, Kepler, Bacon, Harvey, Descartes and Galileo: nature tested by experiment and written in mathematics.

units.title: Philosophers
units.blurb: Descartes' doubt, Hobbes' Leviathan and Spinoza's Ethics.

units.title: Pascal
units.blurb: The vacuum and the arithmetic triangle, the Provincial Letters and the Pensées.

units.title: Poets and Playwrights
units.blurb: Milton's epic, Molière's comedies and Racine's tragedies.

units.title: Newton and Huygens
units.blurb: The laws of motion and gravity, light as a wave, and light split into colors.

topics.title: Gilbert: On the Loadstone
topics.short: Experiments with magnets and a small magnetic globe show that the Earth itself is a great magnet.

topics.title: Bacon: The Advancement of Learning
topics.short: A survey of everything people know, what is missing, and why learning is worth the effort.

topics.title: Kepler: The Harmonies of the World
topics.short: Music in the planets' motions, and in the middle of it the third law: periods and distances fit one rule.

topics.title: Kepler: Epitome of Copernican Astronomy
topics.short: A textbook of the new astronomy: ellipses, equal areas in equal times, and a force from the sun.

topics.title: Bacon: Novum Organum
topics.short: A new method for science: clear away the 'idols' of the mind, gather careful observations, and reason up from them.

topics.title: Bacon: New Atlantis
topics.short: Sailors find an island whose wise men run a great house of research for the good of all.

topics.title: Harvey: On the Motion of the Heart and Blood
topics.short: The heart is a pump, and the same blood goes round and round: proved by experiment and simple arithmetic.

topics.title: Descartes: Discourse on the Method
topics.short: Four rules for thinking clearly, 'I think, therefore I am', and a plan for a science built from the ground up.

topics.title: Descartes: The Geometry
topics.short: Algebra meets geometry: lengths become numbers and curves become equations, the road to the graphs every student draws.

topics.title: Galileo: Two New Sciences
topics.short: Three friends talk through the strength of beams and the laws of falling bodies, tested on inclined planes.

topics.title: Harvey: On the Generation of Animals
topics.short: How a chick takes shape day by day inside the egg, and Harvey's claim that all animals begin from an egg.

topics.title: Descartes: Meditations on First Philosophy
topics.short: Six days of thinking: doubt everything, find what can't be doubted, and rebuild knowledge from there.

topics.title: Hobbes: Leviathan
topics.short: Without government, life would be a war of all against all; so people agree to a strong sovereign.

topics.title: Spinoza: Ethics
topics.short: Philosophy set out like Euclid, with definitions and proofs, on God, nature, the emotions and freedom.

topics.title: Pascal: The Scientific Treatises
topics.short: A barometer carried up a mountain, the push of water in a closed vessel, and the triangle of numbers.
topics.trouble: Rows and places of the triangle are counted from 0; the barometer measures the weight of the air above it, not suction.

topics.title: Pascal: The Provincial Letters
topics.short: Eighteen witty open letters in a religious dispute of his day, which helped shape French prose.

topics.title: Pascal: Pensées
topics.short: Notes for a defense of the Christian faith: the thinking reed, the wager and 'the heart has its reasons.'

topics.title: Milton: Paradise Lost
topics.short: An epic of Satan's rebellion and the fall of Adam and Eve, written by a blind poet to 'justify the ways of God to men.'

topics.title: Milton: Areopagitica and the Poems
topics.short: A famous argument against censoring books before they are printed, with Milton's shorter poems and his drama of Samson.

topics.title: Molière: The Comedies
topics.short: A hypocrite, a miser, a snob and a man who thinks he is sick: comedy that laughs people out of their follies.

topics.title: Racine: Berenice and Phaedra
topics.short: French tragedy at its strictest: one day, one place, and passions that duty can't master.

topics.title: Huygens: Treatise on Light
topics.short: Light as a wave spreading through space, each point sending out its own small wavelets.
topics.trouble: Huygens's waves are pulses with no wavelength, so his theory explains bending but not color.

topics.title: Newton: The Principia
topics.short: Three laws of motion and one law of gravity explain falling apples, the tides and the orbits of the planets.
topics.trouble: Newton's "motion" means momentum, and the Principia is written in geometry, not in the F = ma of today's textbooks.

topics.title: Newton: Optics
topics.short: White light split by a prism into colors and put back together, and the questions Newton left for later science.
topics.trouble: The prism sorts colors that are already in white light; it does not add them.
